item.title: Self-Hosted FOIA Request Systems: Alaveteli vs Froide — Open-Source Freedom of Information Platforms
item.description:
Introduction

Freedom of Information (FOI) laws exist in over 120 countries, giving citizens the legal right to request government documents and data. However, the process of making and tracking FOI requests has traditionally been cumbersome—involving paper forms, email chains, and opaque review processes. Open-source FOI platforms digitize this workflow, making it easier for citizens to submit requests and for government agencies to manage and respond to them.

item.title: Self-Hosted Legal Document Intelligence: OpenContracts vs DocAssemble vs DocLense — Guide 2026
item.description:
Why Self-Host Legal Document Intelligence?

Legal document analysis has traditionally been the domain of expensive enterprise software — tools like Kira Systems, Luminance, and Relativity cost thousands per seat per month. Open-source alternatives have matured dramatically, offering contract analysis, document assembly, and legal intelligence capabilities that rival commercial solutions at zero licensing cost.
